items.note: Compares human-generated alternate-uses ideas with ideas from six chatbots (incl. GPT-3/4), rated by humans and an AI; no participant uses AI, and the abstract gives no human sample size.

Five-sentence stories from 60 LLMs and 60 people are compared on novelty, surprise, diversity, and rated creativity; no human-with-AI condition, so the Holzner et al. CD03 coding as people with vs without AI looks wrong.

Pre-registered study randomly assigns participants to human-human pairs (68 pairs) or human-GPT-4o pairs (72 pairs) on AUT and short-story tasks, scoring originality and diversity of humans' own responses; n = 208 is my count of people (136 + 72) from pair counts, check in full text; the comparison is AI partner vs human partner.

Naturalistic study of 263 students writing short stories with and without ChatGPT, scoring originality and semantic similarity (diversity); assignment mechanism unclear (possibly within-person), check in full text; abstract from the OSF PsyArXiv record.
Compares human output with GPT-4 output under naive and expert prompting on text, drawing, and alternative-uses tasks, scored by external raters and NLP measures; no participant uses AI.

225 university students do a creative writing task with ChatGPT or as a no-ChatGPT control; output creativity (frequency, flexibility) is scored along with surveys; assignment method not stated in the abstract.

Compares pre-LLM student product ideas with GPT-4 zero-shot and few-shot ideas on purchase intent, novelty, and pairwise similarity; no participant uses AI; abstract read from the Wharton working-paper PDF (no DOI); related to Girotra et al. 'Ideas are dimes a dozen'.
600 short stories from human participants and GPT-3 (plus 120 GPT-4 stories) are rated for creativity and analyzed with semantic-distance measures; no participant uses AI.

Studies 1-2 relate question-asking complexity to problem solving in humans (N = 89, 100); Study 3 has 100 AI agents do the same tasks and compares AI and human originality; no participant uses AI; abstract from the OSF preprint.

Quasi-experiment with 80 postgraduates writing an innovative research proposal while interacting with a GAI chatbot versus peers; practical performance on the output is scored, but whether it is a creativity measure needs the full text; non-random assignment and under 50 per arm is possible.
